rounds.fact: GameSpot launched in 1996 and became known for its numerical review scores becoming a genuine influence on game sales, sometimes controversially so.
Salon launched in 1995 as one of the first online-only magazines with no print edition at all, betting entirely on the web as a legitimate home for serious journalism.
RadioShack's website in the early 2000s tried to combine its parts-and-electronics heritage with early attempts at cell phone retail, a business mix that never quite gelled online.
Barnes & Noble launched bn.com in 1997 specifically to compete with Amazon, one of the first major traditional retailers to take online bookselling seriously.
Fark built its entire identity around submitting and voting on weird, funny news links, a simple format that predated Reddit's rise by several years.
